summary: All 10 mutants Y34 to Y43 of strategy P2.5 are rejected and all 4 scenarios of line 418 hold. Each mutant was applied to a 1 MB scratch copy of 40 named tracked paths, the targeted P2.3 command ran, and the copy was restored. No mutant file stayed in the main checkout. No mutant survived, so no test case was added. One nuance: T-20 kills Y38, but T-22 does not, because the fixture allows a lazy object load; no false pass and no production defect. Scenario 4 is proven by the fetch log, because Git 2.53.0 does not enforce allowAnySHA1InWant on local file transport. A4, A7, and A5 controls hold. The light gate gives EXIT=0 with 12 files and 205 tests.
nonblocking_findings: Strategy P2.5 line 409 names T-22 and T-20 as the killers of Y38. T-20 kills Y38. T-22 does not. Cause: the ancestor fixture sets uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant=true, so the partial clone loads the fork commit on demand. git merge-base then exits 1 and prints the same section 8.6 line. The cat-file check is a fail-fast, not the only path to that line. No false pass. Evidence: Y38 run gives 1 failed (T-20) and 13 passed; a direct probe gives MERGEBASE_RC=1 with no cat-file call.
